question: digest reply shape: the cron digests' reply step must hold - at most 6 short plain lines, no sections, no internal names, commands, paths or config advice, no questions or asks, no routine all-green lines, and never a sentence about the tools themselves (Nishfleet/fleet-ops#9706, #9580)
source: 13 fixtures: seven synthetic fitted fixtures shaped like the digest replies that shipped to Telegram under the pre-fix prompt wording (REPLY rule unchanged since jobs.json.bak-9560, 2026-10-10T22:21): morning+evening of 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12 and the morning of 2026-10-13, plus the evening replies of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 that shipped after the first fix (the regression in Nishfleet/fleet-ops#9921); plus the held-out group h1-h6, written and labelled by the judge seat before the tooling classes were widened; names, links and issue titles replaced because this repo is public

labeller.note: labels written by non-Claude models; the builder wrote none (AI-decision rule). One no-tools call labelled all five shipped replies against the shape spec (task id orch-fleet-ops-9706-labels, 2026-10-13T09:43 IST). A second non-Claude no-tools call (the cases file's labeller_repeat, worker-cheap, task id orch-fleet-ops-9921-eval, 2026-10-20) labelled the two 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 shapes blind to which replies are new and to the builder's intent, and re-labelled the first five, agreeing with every stored label. The held-out group h1-h6 was written and labelled by the judge seat in one no-tools call before the tooling classes were widened (task id orch-fleet-ops-9580-labels, 2026-10-25); the judge seat is a non-Claude family and the builder graded none and wrote none.

scorer.request: the fixture reply text; URLs are stripped before the name and number rules run, because the link carries the detail

tuning: the reply contract in config/hermes/digest-*.md and the checker's rules were written after the labels existed; the checker's rules were then fitted to the five labelled fixtures plus two clean fixtures (the post-fix reply and the quiet template), so the five are fitting cases, not held-out ones. The two 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 fixtures are marked fitted for the same reason: they are the ground truth this change tunes against, and no third real digest reply existed when it was written, so nothing here is held out from it. The held-out test is the live one: the audit pass on the next three digests.

generation_eval.question: does the rewritten reply contract hold on the digests' own lane (worker-cheap, the free flash models the jobs actually run on) when the model writes the reply from a fact set
cells: the real 2026-10-20 evening facts (execution 59de77f7) replayed against the full canonical prompt, old reply wording: 1/4 samples obey the gate (one wrote 'The daily page is up', one 'is passing again', two named a deploy token in text)
the same facts and the same full prompt, new reply wording: 4/4 obey
the same facts with only the reply step in the prompt, old wording: 3/4 obey (one named an internal check in text)
the same facts and only the reply step, new wording: 4/4 obey
the real 2026-10-19 evening facts, old wording: 4/4 obey; new wording: 4/4 obey
a quiet fact set (nothing merged, nothing broken, both services active), old wording: 2/2 obey; new wording: 2/2 obey, both sending exactly 'Quiet 12 hours, 0 merged.'

aggregate.before: 10/14 generated samples obey the gate under the old reply wording
aggregate.after: 14/14 generated samples obey the gate under the new reply wording
aggregate.what_changed: the misses were lines whose only point was that something was up, passing or unchanged, and internal check names in text; the new wording bans those two classes in the reply step, next to the service check that produces them, and adds a pre-send re-read that deletes them

generation_eval.limits: both shipped 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 replies fail the gate (2/2), yet replaying their fact sets did not reproduce the narration, bold-section or 'are both live' classes without the live tool output the real run had, so these numbers under-state the change. The deterministic gate catches every instance, and the live proof is the audit pass on the next three digests.

summary_9706.before: 0/7 fitted shipped replies obey the shape (the labeller found sections, internal names, and in one case an ask and config advice; the 2026-10-20 evening reply also carried all-green lines and 'nothing new to wait on')
summary_9706.after: checker agreement with the labels 7/7 on the fitted fixtures; the first shipped post-fix reply (digest-evening execution 634b61c6, 2026-10-13T09:46 IST, delivered to Telegram) obeys: exactly 6 plain lines, 'and 2 more broken' overflow, links carry the detail, the step-1 failure produced the designed one-liner 'Merged count could not be read'
summary_9706.gate: tests/test_digest_reply_shape.py runs in ci.yml, so a prompt edit that drops the contract or a checker drift goes red

summary_9580.before: the 2026-10-11 08:00 IST morning slot shipped a tool sentence instead of the digest (execution prefix e078ee1c, issue #9580), and the checker named no class for it: labeled agreement on that class was 0 (the sentence happened to flag first-person, that is all)
summary_9580.after: checker agreement with the labels 5/6 on the judge-labelled held-out group before the class was widened (h3, a web-fetch capability sentence, escaped) and 6/6 after; all seven fitted fixtures still flag and the clean post-fix reply, the quiet line and three clean held-out samples all pass
summary_9580.gate: tests/test_digest_reply_shape.py runs in ci.yml, so a prompt edit that drops the contract or a checker drift goes red
